claim_ceiling: doctor refuses an unresolvable or tampered component with a typed code; nothing about release, installation or acceptance is claimed
notes: Root cause: _module_source called __import__ directly, so a component named in stack.json with no importable module raised ModuleNotFoundError. That is an ImportError, not an SBLError, and doctor only caught SBLError.
Fix 1: _module_source converts ImportError into SBLError with code SBL_E_COMPONENT_UNRESOLVED and carries the module name, so load, invoke and upgrade also get typed refusals instead of tracebacks.

Fix 2: doctor collects a code per problem and sets report code when problems is non-empty. SBL_E_COMPONENT_UNRESOLVED wins if present, otherwise the first code. ok stays false and problems, target, components, claim_ceiling, host_install_state keep their shape.
The missing-manifest early return also gained a code (SBL_E_NOT_INSTALLED) so every non-ok doctor payload is typed, matching the code regex the tests assert.
Codes introduced: SBL_E_COMPONENT_UNRESOLVED, SBL_E_DIGEST_MISMATCH, SBL_E_MANIFEST_INCOMPLETE, SBL_E_CORE_UNHEALTHY, SBL_E_NOT_INSTALLED.
Tests were not edited, no other module was touched, and no commits were made.
Observed but not chased (budget): this repo's pytest config prints no trailing counts line, so the numbers here come from the nine per-test result characters and the PASSED listing.
